callee_callers.note: Full .text scan for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on 0x5228fe0. The entry window's own call site 0x514b0ff is one of the twelve. Indirect calls, tail jumps and PLT references are not claimed by this scan.
callee_callers.scan_note: This census is for the callee, not the entry: the entry window itself has zero direct e8 callers (see incoming).

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses. The ELF section table maps .text at VA 0x1343c80, file offset 0x1342c80, size 0x431c430; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. Tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming.note: Full .text scan for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on 0x514b0f0 finds none. Reach via indirect call, vtable slot or tail jump is not established and not claimed; the window's own protocol (rsi = out pointer, rdx = object base) is what the entry bytes show.

rule.callee_full_value: The callee's full rax is NOT a clean 0/1: mov loads the 32-bit field zero-extended, and setg rewrites only the low byte, so callee rax = (field & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFF00) | low, where low is 1 iff field > 0 signed. The entry's movzbl %al,%eax discards those upper bytes, which is what makes the composed output exactly 0 or 1.
rule.composed: out = 1 iff int32 at [rdx + 0x1100] > 0 (signed comparison); otherwise out = 0. Return value is 1 on every path. rbx is preserved and the stack is balanced (one push, one pop, no rsp adjustment).
rule.field_type: The callee reads a 32-bit field (mov (%rdi),%eax + test %eax,%eax + setg), so the comparison is signed 32-bit: field 0x80000000 is -2147483648, not a large positive. A 64-bit read would change the verdict for fields whose low 32 bits are positive but whose high 32 bits set the sign; no such read exists in either window.
